post.caption:
Transmission losses depend on current, not voltage, so the trick is to send power at enormous voltage and tiny current and step it back down at the far end. Transformers do that, and transformers only work on current that keeps reversing. Direct current could not be stepped up at the time, which is the real reason AC won, not safety or showmanship. The twist: modern power electronics made high-voltage DC efficient, and the biggest transmission projects now use it.
